evidence.exact_quote: Every runtime, bridged-provider, and permission-facing envelope that carries account identity must preserve:

items.impact: Consumers can distinguish requested intent from the identity that actually executed across runtime and permission surfaces.
items.statement: The owner contract requires requested account id, policy, binding, effective account id, effective provider identity, execution role, and operational identity to propagate together.
items.title: Requested and effective identity envelope

evidence.exact_quote: secrets remain outside config/state stores; actual `/tokens/keys` remain only in OS credential storage.

items.impact: Canonical state can reference credentials without becoming a secret store.
items.statement: Stable PM account identity and non-secret credential references are separated from provider-native identity and credential material.
items.title: Stable identity and secret-storage boundary

evidence.exact_quote: Switching happens only at attempt/message boundaries. Never switch mid-attempt.
Scheduler switch records MUST persist stable reason codes rather than UI-only text.

items.impact: Attempt ownership is deterministic and failover decisions are auditable by stable machine-readable reasons.
items.statement: Account switching is boundary-scoped, sticky, and reason-coded; a completed attempt remains attributed to its actual account.
items.title: Boundary-scoped reason-coded rotation

evidence.exact_quote: The `/hard` no-fallback rule is explicit: no-fallback applies when the request names an explicit `auth-mode`, when manual preferred-account override or `Set Preferred` is active as `/control`, when policy disallows fallback, when the current selectable unit is in cooldown or hard block, when account readiness is `needs_configuration` or `validation_required`, when credentials are invalid or missing, or when no eligible backup account exists.
Auto-switch is allowed when policy permits and one of these occurs:

items.impact: Implementations could either fail over or block on the same cooldown or hard-block condition, producing divergent runtime behavior and misleading recovery UI.
items.statement: The no-fallback paragraph includes current-unit cooldown or hard block as reasons to prohibit fallback, while adjacent rotation rules make hard exhaustion, cooldown, and temporary unavailability triggers for fallback; precedence is not reconciled.
items.title: Cooldown and hard-block fallback contradiction

evidence.exact_quote: `status` is the user-facing lifecycle summary and closes to `active | expired | revoked | error`.

items.impact: Builders must invent how lifecycle status relates to availability, configuration, credential, health, pressure, and setup states, risking contradictory chips and routing eligibility.
items.statement: The four-value user-facing status enum is defined without a complete projection or precedence table for the other first-class state dimensions declared in the same account model.
items.title: Lifecycle status projection lacks precedence

evidence.exact_quote: Across all CLI-backed providers, `auth_state`, `history`, `mcp_oauth_tokens`, `extensions runtime state`, `project registry`, `temp chats`, `workspace_trust`, `runtime_cache`, `cooldown_residue`, and `telemetry_state` are denied from sharing by default.

items.impact: Account-bearing state and residue do not leak between runnable CLI profiles by default.
items.statement: PM-owned provider and account roots isolate auth, history, trust, runtime caches, sessions, and provider-generated state while permitting only explicit target-specific overlays.
items.title: CLI account-root isolation and deny-by-default sharing

evidence.exact_quote: A persistent `Effective Runtime` inspector remains visible in the provider detail flow and predicts the likely requested/effective runtime before launch.

items.impact: Users can inspect likely resolution and later distinguish it from actual execution identity.
items.statement: Agent-Config has a fixed section order and a persistent Effective Runtime inspector with account/profile health, pressure, and resolution disclosure.
items.title: Persistent effective-runtime disclosure

evidence.exact_quote: `Logged in` is not the same as `Ready`.

items.impact: Authentication success cannot falsely advertise an account as schedulable before configuration and entitlement checks pass.
items.statement: Setup and remediation distinguish login, configuration, validation, readiness, expiry, failure, logout, and disabled states.
items.title: Authentication and readiness are separate

evidence.exact_quote: **Remove account/profile:** present a confirmation dialog with `Remove from PM only` and `Remove and archive PM-managed data` choices. Both choices remove the account/profile record and reassign any threads or defaults pointing at that account/profile; only the archive choice captures PM-managed artifacts first.

items.impact: A crash or concurrent run during archive, record deletion, or reference reassignment could leave dangling defaults, incomplete archives, or unclear retained-data obligations.
items.statement: Removal names user choices and broad effects but does not define transaction ordering, in-flight-run handling, rollback, archive verification, retention, or archive deletion semantics.
items.title: Account removal lacks atomic recovery and data lifecycle

evidence.exact_quote: Each row shows:

provider `/account/profile` list rows stay dense for scan-friendly `/layout`; detailed usage `/cooldown` and requested `/effective` explanation belongs in the persistent inspector rather than overloading the list row.

items.impact: Dense rows, state chips, inspectors, and action labels may be inaccessible or fail under translated expansion without testable requirements.
items.statement: The detailed GUI contract does not specify keyboard order, screen-reader naming, non-color state cues, focus recovery, text scaling, or localization/overflow behavior.
items.title: GUI accessibility and localization are unowned

evidence.exact_quote: PM validates the key with a lightweight test API call such as `list models` or the provider's nearest equivalent.

items.impact: API-key setup has a concrete success probe, secure storage handoff, and recoverable error path.
items.statement: API-key registration requires secure entry, a lightweight provider validation call, OS credential storage, and concrete failure reasons.
items.title: API-key registration oracle

evidence.exact_quote: PM polls for the token every 5 seconds with a total timeout of 5 minutes.

items.impact: Providers can throttle or reject polling, cancellation can race late success, and app restart/network loss may strand authorization state or duplicate account creation.
items.statement: The fixed device-code polling cadence and timeout omit provider `slow_down` handling, jitter/backoff, cancellation, restart/resume, duplicate callback, and late-token acceptance rules.
items.title: Device-code polling lacks race and restart semantics

evidence.exact_quote: No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks are created.

items.impact: The standardized PlanUnit preserves owner vocabulary without silently becoming executable work.
items.statement: MA-002 explicitly confines itself to owner requirements, source preservation, and terminology boundaries.
items.title: MA-002 preserves the planning boundary

evidence.exact_quote: Account/profile rows preserve route-specific auth, billing, region, entitlement, quota, and transport differences.

items.impact: Distinct commercial, regional, auth, and transport routes cannot be collapsed into misleading generic accounts.
items.statement: MA-062 requires separate provider route credential/profile rows when auth, billing, region, entitlement, quota, transport, support, or proof custody differs.
items.title: Route-specific provider profile separation

evidence.exact_quote: Direct-provider usage and entitlement checks are tied to the correct provider/account route.

items.impact: Usage and blocked-state reporting reflect the correct upstream authority instead of optional CLI failures or generic provider errors.
items.statement: MA-063 binds subscription, entitlement, and usage authority to each direct-provider route and requires concrete gating reasons.
items.title: Provider-specific usage authority

evidence.exact_quote: Multi-account routing remains shared provider-runtime behavior rather than Orchestrator-only behavior.

items.impact: All provider-using actor families inherit the same routing contract without reviving retired inventory assumptions.
items.statement: MA-003 establishes an open-ended provider catalog spanning direct, CLI-runtime, and server-bridge routes for all provider-using roles.
items.title: Open-ended shared provider-runtime scope

evidence.exact_quote: Requested and effective provider/account identity remain visible and queryable.

items.impact: Policy and execution identity remain inspectable while secrets and routing ownership stay correctly bounded.
items.statement: MA-004 locks default-on auto-switching, project-owned policy snapshots, requested/effective disclosure, Provider-owned wiring, and secret exclusion.
items.title: Effective policy visibility and storage alignment

evidence.exact_quote: Usage remains the owner for account pressure and quota-pressure projection.

items.impact: Routing and settings consume one pressure model instead of diverging quota subsystems.
items.statement: MA-005 binds account-pool selection, fallback, thresholds, pressure, operator history, and GUI disclosure to the Usage-owned pressure model.
items.title: Account pool consumes Usage-owned pressure

evidence.exact_quote: Behavior-driving facts remain distinct from audit-only facts.

items.impact: Recovery evidence stays auditable without allowing consumer documents or provider-native labels to seize account ownership.
items.statement: MA-006 preserves recovery consumers, actor/target separation, storage audit identity, behavior-driving flags, and shared-runtime ownership boundaries.
items.title: Recovery audit owner boundary

evidence.exact_quote: Distinct actor/run kinds share account truth without collapsing ontologies.

items.impact: Account truth propagates across actor types while historical and active identity remain distinguishable.
items.statement: MA-007 applies requested/effective account identity to conversations, interviews, builders, nodes, attempts, documents, reviews, and serialization without feature-local account state.
items.title: Cross-actor account identity propagation

evidence.exact_quote: Reference table rows remain traceable.
External references are design evidence and do not become PM owner docs.

items.impact: Traceable but stale external behavior could be treated as sufficient design proof after provider APIs, auth flows, or rate-limit semantics change.
items.statement: MA-008 preserves external evidence inventory and a sufficiency assessment but defines no freshness, primary-source reconciliation, or executable conformance oracle for that evidence.
items.title: External evidence sufficiency can drift

evidence.exact_quote: provider_account_id remains provider-native metadata rather than canonical identity.

items.impact: Cross-surface consumers can preserve stable internal identity and actor context without confusing provider-native handles for canonical accounts.
items.statement: MA-009 defines the requested/effective envelope and subordinates provider_account_id to canonical stable account identity.
items.title: Canonical account identity envelope

evidence.exact_quote: Stale CLI-centric assumptions for Codex and GitHub Copilot are not revived.

items.impact: Provider implementations use current direct-provider and account-isolation boundaries instead of retired CLI assumptions.
items.statement: MA-010 explicitly corrects Codex and Copilot routing, Cursor HOME/XDG isolation, and Gemini quota project-context identity.
items.title: Provider inventory canon correction

evidence.exact_quote: Storage alignment remains redb plus seglog, with temporary JSON only as an interim app-data option.

items.impact: Account state and events have bounded owners while historical UI lineage cannot authorize legacy application recreation.
items.statement: MA-011 assigns registry/cooldown/cache state to redb or interim app-data JSON, events to seglog, and provider wiring to the Provider contract.
items.title: Rewrite-era storage and provider alignment

evidence.exact_quote: Concrete provider_entry_id is not replaced by provider_family_id.

items.impact: Runtime, auth, regional, and billing boundaries remain explicit even when provider families are pooled for policy or display.
items.statement: MA-012 preserves concrete provider entries, additive family metadata, transport kinds, supported auth surfaces, and vendor-specific coding-plan endpoints.
items.title: Provider-entry and coding-plan identity boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: account_id remains the internal stable key.

items.impact: Provider-native identity changes cannot destabilize PM joins, and auth families with different quota semantics remain distinct rows.
items.statement: MA-013 locks stable account identity, additive health fields, non-secret credential references, lifecycle status, and auth-family separation.
items.title: Stable account-profile schema

evidence.exact_quote: credential_ref remains a pointer and never the secret itself.

items.impact: Credential attachment can be validated before runtime without serializing secret material into account records.
items.statement: MA-014 defines non-secret credential store handles and provider-declared credential-consumption surfaces with early compatibility validation.
items.title: Credential reference and auth-surface validation

evidence.exact_quote: query_param remains deprecated and warns before use.

items.impact: API keys placed in URLs can leak through logs, traces, proxy history, referrers, crash reports, and support exports even if the UI warns first.
items.statement: Deprecation and a warning are specified for query-parameter credentials, but prohibition criteria, redaction, telemetry suppression, and retention controls are not.
items.title: Query-parameter credentials lack leak controls

segments.summary: Reviewed the canonical identity envelope, account schema, credential boundary, selectable-unit resolution, and rotation policy; found a material cooldown/fallback contradiction and an incomplete lifecycle-state projection.

Reviewed signal thresholds, provider-specific account isolation, routing consumers, Agent-Config, setup states, and destructive account controls; found missing transaction/retention and accessibility/localization contracts.
Reviewed registration/auth flows, usage and instruction projections, owner boundaries, MA-002, MA-003, MA-062, and MA-063; found incomplete device-code race, throttling, and restart semantics.

Reviewed MA-004 through MA-009 for effective policy, Usage ownership, recovery audit boundaries, actor propagation, evidence inventory, and identity envelopes; found no freshness or conformance oracle for external evidence sufficiency.

Reviewed MA-010 through MA-014 for provider canon correction, storage alignment, provider-entry identity, account-profile schema, and credential surfaces; found query-parameter credential leak controls under-specified.

cross_document_questions: Which owner contract resolves the contradiction between cooldown or hard-block no-fallback and cooldown or hard-exhaustion failover?
Which storage or account-lifecycle owner defines atomic account removal, in-flight-run handling, archive verification, retention, and rollback?
Which GUI owner supplies keyboard, assistive-technology, non-color, scaling, and localization requirements for dense account rows and inspectors?
Which auth owner prohibits or fully redacts query-parameter credentials across logs, traces, proxies, crash reports, and support bundles?
research_queries: Current OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant polling error, slow_down, cancellation, and restart requirements
Current provider-specific account usage and entitlement APIs cited by the Multi-Account evidence inventory
Security guidance for API keys in URL query parameters and end-to-end observability redaction
